extraction_scope: Mirror of source-reviewed mechanism ontology record.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: WN53, WN83, and DN59 inhibit flavivirus infectivity in plaque-reduction assays, supporting an entry-stage antiviral phenotype under the reported preincubation/removal assay design.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: WN53, WN83, DN59 and related tested peptides
mechanism_claims.limitations: The assay measures infection/focus reduction after virus-peptide preincubation; it does not identify a direct peptide binding site or molecular target.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=4:Identification of Flavivirus inhibitory peptides; xml:sec=5:Determination of 50% inhibitory concentrations; xml:sec=13:Viral plaque reduction assays

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The source supports sequence-specific inhibition because scrambled DN59/WN83 controls and SINV controls did not show significant inhibition under the reported conditions.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: DN59, WN83, WN53 and scrambled controls
mechanism_claims.limitations: Specificity controls reduce the likelihood of nonspecific virion/cell toxicity but still do not prove the exact structural interaction.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The authors propose that DN59, WN53, and WN83 may interfere with intramolecular interactions between flavivirus E stem/domain regions during class II fusion-protein rearrangement.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is an author-proposed mechanism based on WWIHS/domain mapping, structural context, and entry phenotype; the paper does not provide direct binding, structural, or fusion-intermediate assays.
